cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: The twelve Olympian gods lived on Mount Olympus and ruled different aspects of the world

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Zeus was king of the gods, god of the sky, thunder and justice; his symbols are the thunderbolt and eagle

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Hera was queen of the gods, goddess of marriage and childbirth; she was famously jealous of Zeus's affairs

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Poseidon was god of the sea, earthquakes and horses; his symbol is the trident

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Athena was goddess of wisdom, warfare strategy and crafts; she was born from Zeus's head fully armed

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Apollo was god of the sun, music, prophecy and healing; his oracle at Delphi was the most important in Greece

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Artemis was goddess of the hunt, wilderness and the moon; she was a virgin goddess who protected young women

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Ares was god of war, representing the brutal and chaotic side of battle; he was not widely worshipped in Greece

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Aphrodite was goddess of love, beauty and desire; she was born from sea-foam according to Hesiod

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: The gods behaved like humans — they argued, fell in love, took revenge and showed favouritism

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: Greek myths explained natural phenomena, human emotions and social customs through divine stories

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Olympian Gods
cards.back: The gods could intervene in human affairs but were subject to the Moirai (Fates)
